subject: Discovery recap: HelioHealth data protection & logging constraints
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Discovery recap: HelioHealth data protection & logging constraints

Hi Olivia — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from my side so we have a shared view and clear next steps.

Meeting highlights / pain points you raised:
- PII exposure risk in generated outputs and logs: need strict redaction or token hashing for identifiable fields (SSNs, MRNs, emails).
- Auditability: security/compliance team requires immutable audit logs with user/context, timestamp, and model/version used for each call.
- Retention windows: primary ask is 30 days for request/response payloads, 365 days for audit metadata (who/when/model), and the ability to shorten retention per dataset on demand.
- No raw prompt storage for PHI workflows; only hashed or tokenized indices allowed for debugging.
- Requirement to support SOC 2 evidence exports and periodic audit extracts (CSV/JSON) for a rolling 12-month window.

Current stack you described:
- Frontend collects clinical notes -> internal API -> Redwood inference endpoints (planned PoC).
- Cloud: GCP (us-west2) with KMS for key management.
- Internal SIEM: Splunk for ingesting logs and alerts.

Success criteria you mentioned:
- Minimal latency impact (<200ms p99 on inference path) with redaction in place for identifiers.
- Demonstrable ability to produce audit exports for a sample week on-demand.
- Contractually acceptable retention and deletion controls (ability to delete customer data on request).

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) I will share a short tech checklist and our recommended config options for redaction + retention (attached: data-retention-options.xlsx).
2) Schedule technical deep dive with your infra/security folks to validate SIEM integration and audit export format — proposed slots next Tue/Wed morning PT.
3) Share a DPA/DPA redline starter and a data handling summary for HelioHealth legal (attached: redwood-dpa-draft.pdf).

Can you confirm: is your legal/infosec point-of-contact Jorge Ramirez (cc'd) the right person to receive the DPA draft? Also, do you want the PoC to run in a Dedicated (isolated GPU pool) or Private VPC deployment for the initial evaluation?

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: HelioHealth data protection & logging constraints

Hi Soojin — thanks for the detailed recap, this matches our notes. A few clarifications and requests from our side: 

Clarifications:
- Retention: 30 days for full request/response is preferred for production PHI flows; we can accept 90 days for non-PHI evaluation traffic. Audit metadata (user, timestamp, model id) must be retained for 365 days.
- Redaction: we need deterministic redaction/hashing for identifiers so we can correlate events without storing raw values. Can Redwood provide both server-side redaction and a client-side SDK helper to fingerprint identifiers before transmission?
- Export format: Splunk-friendly newline-delimited JSON for audit exports and a CSV option for legal review.

Requests / constraints:
- Legal insists on an option to run the PoC in a Private deployment (VPC) due to PHI exposure during initial testing. Will need a rough order-of-magnitude cost and a short list of required network egress/IP ranges.
- SLA conversation: our procurement team will need contract language around data deletion timelines and an ability to request data destruction with certification.

Next steps from our side:
- Jorge (cc) will take the DPA draft and loop in procurement/legal for early redlines.
- Jorge / infra will confirm availability for a technical call next Tue (06 Apr) or Thu (08 Apr). Morning PT works best.

Thanks — Olivia
Olivia Grant
